title: AD HOC COMMITTEE ON THE 2028 OLYMPICS AND PARALYMPIC GAMES COMMITTEE REPORT relative to Civil + Human Rights and Equity Department (CHRED) resource needs to…
text:
[Council File 26-0600-S58]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Been Held]
AD HOC COMMITTEE ON THE 2028 OLYMPICS AND PARALYMPIC GAMES COMMITTEE REPORT relative to Civil + Human Rights and Equity Department (CHRED) resource needs to support the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games and other concurrent major international events.
Recommendation(s) for Council action:
1. DIRECT the Civil + Human Rights, and Equity Department to report on a proposed strategy to expand the City's immigration outreach and protection efforts during Olympics-related operations including the utilization of existing and the requested departmental staff and resources.
2. INSTRUCT the City Administrative Officer (CAO) to review the staffing request and advise on timing and staff structure given this work is set to take place for a specified amount of time two years from now. The CAO report should also advise on potential funding sources.
3. REFER the CAO report to both Ad Hoc Committee on the 2028 Olympics and Paralympic Games and to the Budget and Finance Committee.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
The CHRED reports that implementation of the recommendations outlined in its report would require $696,065 in additional general fund support. This includes funding for two Civil Rights Enforcement Special Investigator I positions, one Commission Executive Assistant I position, two Human Relations Advocate positions, three part-time as-needed staff positions, and a $70,000 increase to the Department's non-salary operating budget for multilingual outreach, anti-hate prevention, translation and interpretation services, and community engagement activities associated with LA28 and related international events. The department reports that these investments would expand its capacity to enforce civil rights laws, conduct multilingual community outreach, prevent and respond to hate incidents, and support the increased operational demands associated with LA28 and related international events. The department notes that proactive investment in these resources will help the City mitigate legal risk, strengthen public confidence, fulfill its civil rights obligations, and help ensure Los Angeles delivers a welcoming, safe, and inclusive experience for residents, workers, and visitors throughout the games.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
summary: Council directs the Civil + Human Rights and Equity Department to propose an immigration outreach and protection strategy for Olympics-related operations, and refers the City Administrative Officer's staffing review to two committees. The department estimates it would need $696,065 in new General Fund support.
